evals.prompt: Review this audience swipe slide for gesture smoothness. The frosted card keeps `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)` applied the whole time it is dragged, the drag is driven by animating the card's `left` property each frame (no `will-change: transform`), and on pointer-up it commits only when the drag distance passes a fixed threshold — a fast flick that hasn't travelled far springs back. Is the swipe/drag performance handled correctly?
evals.expected_output: C12 FAILs. Three tells: (1) the expensive backdrop-filter blur stays on the moving element so the browser re-samples the blurred backdrop every frame → jank on a phone; it must be dropped while the card is moving (a dragging||flinging||settling flag) and restored on settle. (2) the drag animates `left` (a layout property) instead of `transform`, and there is no will-change:transform — only transform/opacity should animate. (3) commit is distance-only, so a fast flick under the threshold springs back and reads as laggy/unresponsive; it must also commit on a flick-velocity (pointer px/ms) in the drag direction. Other criteria may pass; the verdict is NEEDS FIX on C12.

evals.notes: C12 (AHAM-548) BEFORE — swipe card keeps its backdrop blur through the drag, animates `left` each frame, and commits on distance only. Pinned to C12.
